newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-NOVOTNA BEATS CAPRIATI IN AMERITECH CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA BEATS CAPRIATI IN AMERITECH CUP FINAL.

text.p: Czech Jana Novotna won her second consecutive tournament Sunday, beating Jennifer Capriati 6-4 3-6 6-1 in the final of the $450,000 Ameritech Cup tournament.

Novotna, number five in the world and coming off a win at Zurich, beat Capriati for the third time this year and then apologised after the match for negative statements she made about the 20-year-old American after beating her in Essen last February.
"I made some negative or critical comments about Jennifer's comeback," Novotna said. "I wanted to give her credit."
"I've heard some things," Capriati said. "I just look at the ball. That's all I care about. I just play the ball."

Capriati, who upset number one Monica Seles in the semifinal round, was appearing in her first final since the Canadian Open in 1993. Her last win was at Sydney earlier that year. She played in one tournament in 1994 and then missed two years because of personal problems and injuries.
She missed a few chances in the first set, reaching break point five times in the 10th game, yet Novotna rallied each time, including two aces, to win the 18-point game.
In the second set, Capriati and Novotna exchanged service breaks in the first two games. Then Capriati held off Novotna who was at break point twice in the third game.
"Whenever I was down, I produced some good serves and that's what made the difference," Novotna said.
Capriati broke Novotna in the sixth game, and frustrated the 28-year-old Czech with back-to-back forehand winners to open the seventh before winning at love and taking a 5-2 lead.

Novotna controlled the third set, committing just seven unforced errors in the set to Capriati's 13. The difference in the match was Capriati finishing 3-for-10 in break point conversions and Novotna's strong net game.
"She has a difficult game to play against," Capriati said. "She doesn't let you get into a rhythm. You've got to be on to beat her."

It was the third tournament win this year for Novotna, who defeated 16-year-old Swiss sensation Martina Hingis in the semifinals. She also won at Madrid as well as Zurich this year, and could move up to number four in the rankings.

"When you have the number one player in the world and Jennifer's comeback and Martina Hingis playing here, it's not surprising that they get all the headlines," Novotna said. "You see in the end, I end up being the winner. I get the headlines tomorrow."
